Topics · The prophets

How did every nation learn what God asks?

Judaism teaches that God's moral claim reaches every nation. The Quran asks next: how did each nation know?

Part 1 of 3

﴿رُّسُلًا مُّبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ حُجَّةٌۢ بَعْدَ ٱلرُّسُلِ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

[We sent] messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners so that mankind will have no argument against Allāh after the messengers. And ever is Allāh Exalted in Might and Wise.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:165

A stranger is brought before a village elder for breaking a rule of the market. She asks one thing first: did anyone tell him? No one had. She sends him on his way with a kind word, and tells the market to post its rules at the gate. The verse says something of this kind: messengers came with good news and warning, so that no one could say: nobody told us.

A question for you

How do you think the nations came to know what God asks of them?

If you sayThrough Noah, handed down
ThenThen knowledge of God began as the property of everyone, which is where the Quran's story begins too: people were one community. A question remains: how does something handed down live for thousands of years with no one to renew it?
If you sayThrough reason and conscience
ThenA strong answer, and the Quran agrees that each soul is given a sense of its own right and wrong. Conscience tells you not to steal. Does it tell you who made you and how to call on Him? The next verses name what was added to conscience.
If you sayThrough Israel, as a light to the nations
ThenA noble calling. The next verses speak also of the centuries before Sinai, and of lands far from Israel.

Translation of the meaning

And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allāh sends astray [thereby] whom He wills[649] and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

Translator's notes

[649] i.e., those who refuse His guidance.

Quran · Ibrahim 14:4

Picture a village on a far coast, a thousand years before anyone there would hear of Moses. An old man stands up in the council and says the market scales are lying, and that the One above sees it. They laugh. A few listen. He is forgotten, and no scripture keeps his name. The Quran says there were many like him, and that only some are named.

A question for you

If messengers came to every nation, what would you expect to find in the world's old traditions?

If you sayTraces of one moral core
ThenThen likeness across cultures is what the claim predicts, and the differences need their own explanation. The Quran offers one, in later Steps.
If you sayNot much; too much is lost
ThenThe verses agree that much is hidden from us. The Quran says it names only some messengers. Its claim is that God was not absent, and it does not promise that we can find the proof.
If you sayOnly what Israel's God revealed to Israel
ThenThat keeps the line of revelation clear. It also leaves the question you began with: what did the nations know, and how?

A question for you
